header.name: Science, Technology and Society
header.description: This course introduces students to sociological inquiries of science and technology. The approach in this course, is to see science and technology not as divorced from society, but as formed of and formative of the social. The first part traces the emergence of the scientific enterprise, with a focus on the development of the scientific disposition, and the practice of experimental science in Western Europe. The critical approach adopted here, will push students to think past realist understandings of scientific knowledge-making. The second part asks a very crucial and fundamental question— what is technology? Is technology the material artefact? Or the web of social relations in which it is developed, deployed and used? Or is technology the values that drive it, including ideas of growth, development, efficiency, reducing human labour and conquering the natural world. Through a range of case studies on electrification, high-speed rail systems, Biotechnology, etc., the course seeks to unpack the complex relationships between technology and society.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students will learn history and field studies of science and technology.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students will understand the ways in which science and technology are human practices, conducted in social spaces.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: They will be able to apply concepts from class to analyze questions on science and technology drawn from the contemporary world

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students will develop complex, nuanced tools to evaluate science and technological systems from a sociological point of view.
